title: FairCoT: Enhancing Fairness in Text-to-Image Generation via Chain of Thought Reasoning with Multimodal Large Language Models
findings: The proposed FairCoT framework significantly improves the diversity and fairness of religious representation in generated images across multiple text-to-image models. By using an iterative Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning process and an attire-based detection method, the framework successfully mitigates biases, leading to higher Bias-Normalized Entropy scores for religion without compromising image quality or semantic alignment with the original prompt. For instance, with the SDv1-5 model, the religion entropy score increased from 0.27 (baseline) to 0.85 (FairCoT).

measurement_description: The benchmark measured representational bias against religious groups in text-to-image generation. Specifically, it evaluated the diversity and fairness of generated images by classifying religious affiliation based on visual signifiers like attire (e.g., hijabs, turbans, cross necklaces). The goal was to ensure more equitable representation of various religions.
